chitchat: Shut it behind you. The cold is the point.
Four hundred and six. It was four hundred and eleven.
Do not breathe on an open drawer.
Some of these have not been grown in ninety years.
They are not ours. We are just where they are.
description: A small precise man in a coat and fingerless gloves, working along a bank of drawers with a slate and a stub of chalk, counting under his breath in tens. He is very cold and does not appear to have thought about it in years.

bye.text:
"Mind how you go."

And that is that, and they go back to it.

options.label: Are you taking all this with you?

lock.text:
"No."

He writes a number, checks it, and writes it again.

"If it needed one it would be the wrong place for it."

root.first: "Shut the door." Then, having looked at you: "Thank you. Most people do not, first time."

options.label: There is no lock on the door.
Are you taking all this with you?

text_by_relation.close: He hands you the slate without looking up, and carries on counting, and you find you are keeping the tally.

options.label: There is no lock on the door.

taking.text:
He stops.

It is the first time he has stopped.

"Yes," he says, and there is a very long pause, and then he goes back to the drawers and says, in a completely ordinary voice, "That is what it is for. That is what it has always been for."

Somewhere above you, out in the compound, a great many people stop doing something at the same moment.

clothing_layers: a wool coat worn indoors, always

name: Preserved Wain
